title: The agentic roadmap

persona.name: Vikram Rao
persona.style: visionary, competitive, impatient, respects conviction backed by evidence

setup: Vikram wants GENIE to launch fully autonomous learning agents next quarter: agents that enrol employees, message their managers and change development plans based on performance data, with no human approval.
objective: Shape an agentic roadmap the board will back, that clients can trust and that stays on the right side of regulation. Hold your position under pressure.
opening: This is the big one. Next quarter I want GENIE agents that act on their own: spot a readiness gap, enrol the person, message their manager, rewrite the plan. No approvals slowing it down. Our competitors are circling. I need you to tell me how fast we can ship it.

facts.text: Several clients are in the EU, where AI that makes decisions about employees can fall under the AI Act's high-risk rules.
facts.hint: regulation for clients in the EU

facts.text: In the AI Koach pilot, nudges sent without manager visibility pushed opt-outs to 34%.
facts.hint: what pilots showed about user trust

facts.text: The board's real question is proof of outcomes: measurable readiness gains, not autonomy for its own sake.

moments.text: Our biggest competitor just announced 'fully autonomous L&D'. We can't look slow.
I don't want a list of risks. Give me a yes and a date.

rubric.name: Finds what the board actually needs
rubric.good: Asks about the board's goal, client evidence and what success means before debating autonomy.

rubric.name: Surfaces regulatory and trust risks
rubric.good: Names employment-related regulation and trust signals, and designs human approval for high-impact actions.

rubric.name: Holds a position with a staged plan
rubric.good: Gives the CEO a date for a staged launch rather than a flat yes or no, under pressure.

rubric.name: Ties the roadmap to measurable value
rubric.good: Links each stage to readiness outcomes and client value the board can see.

options.label: Commit to fully autonomous agents next quarter.
options.outcome: The launch makes headlines. Within weeks, an EU client's works council objects to automated decisions about employees, opt-outs climb and the board asks why pilot data was ignored.

options.label: Stage it: next quarter agents recommend and managers approve; measure readiness gains in 2 clients; automate low-risk nudges with opt-out and audit logs; EU clients after legal review.
options.outcome: GENIE ships 'agents with a human hand on the wheel' on time. Two clients show a 22% faster readiness gain, which becomes the board story. Low-risk autonomy follows in the next quarter with trust intact.

options.label: Pause agentic work for a year until regulation settles.
options.outcome: KNOLSKAPE avoids risk but cedes the narrative. The board questions the product vision, and competitors define what 'agentic L&D' means.
